article.audio.title: Musical instrument classification – Deep Learning
article.audio.subtitle: Complete audio classification pipeline with signal cleaning, MFCC extraction, CNN training, and prediction using temporal windows.
article.audio.overview.title: Goal
article.audio.overview.text: Automatically recognize a musical instrument from an audio file. Audio is a continuous temporal signal, and the core of the project is transforming the raw waveform into a robust representation, then training a deep learning model capable of generalizing across recording variations.
article.audio.dataset.title: Data
article.audio.dataset.text: The dataset comes from a Kaggle competition focused on musical instruments. Each audio file is labeled (piano, guitar, violin, drums, etc.). The main challenges are recording variability and class imbalance between some instruments.
article.audio.preprocessing.title: Preprocessing and EDA
article.audio.preprocessing.text: Before training, the audio is processed in several ways: temporal signal, FFT, filter banks, and MFCCs. Envelope-based signal cleaning is used to automatically remove silence and keep only meaningful segments.
article.audio.features.text: MFCCs are used as model inputs. They summarize useful frequency information while producing a 2D representation (time × coefficients) that can be processed efficiently by a convolutional network.
article.audio.model.title: Model
article.audio.model.text: The classifier is a Keras CNN composed of multiple convolution layers, max pooling, dropout, and dense layers. The idea is to learn local patterns inside the MFCC representation (similarly to an image), then aggregate this information to predict the instrument.
article.audio.training.title: Training and results
article.audio.training.text: Training is performed on randomly sampled audio windows in order to increase the diversity of examples seen by the network. Class weighting is applied to reduce the impact of underrepresented classes. The model reaches an accuracy of around 93%.
article.audio.prediction.title: Prediction
article.audio.prediction.text: During inference, the audio is split into successive windows, each window is converted into MFCCs, normalized the same way as during training, and passed through the model. Probabilities are then averaged across the whole file to produce a more stable prediction. Results are exported into a CSV file.
article.audio.conclusion.title: Conclusion and future work
article.audio.conclusion.text: The project covers the whole pipeline, meaning signal processing, feature engineering, deep learning, and inference. Possible next steps include audio data augmentation, full mel spectrograms, or CRNN architectures (CNN + RNN).
